A model predicts that a 50% improvement in tax productivity could raise long-run GDP per capita in low-income countries by about 18% on average. The authors argue that reforms should focus on the productivity of tax authorities rather than their size, noting that practices like using third-party data and digital tools rely more on organizational capability than large budgets.
items.title: New research links tax collection efficiency to economic growth in low-income countries

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police announced plans to curb air pollution following an inter-state coordination meeting. Measures include creating a dedicated WhatsApp group for real-time coordination, diverting non-compliant inter-city buses at borders, and enforcing entry restrictions for vehicles registered outside Delhi from November 1 to January 31. Special Commissioner Ajay Chaudhry emphasized improved stakeholder coordination, while Deputy Commissioner SK Singh highlighted public awareness and strict enforcement of emission norms.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Plans New Measures to Curb Air Pollution

items.summary: A Singapore High Court ordered car dealer Ong Bee Hong to pay rival Wu Chong $300,000 regarding an aborted Lamborghini deal. Although Wu successfully proved Ong falsely claimed to have found a buyer for a Ferrari, Wu's own claims for damages were dismissed because he failed to prove specific financial losses. Justice Kristy Tan noted that while Ong remained legally obliged to pay Wu $250,000 under a separate genuine sales agreement, he refused to deduct this amount from the counter-claim award. The judge urged Ong to act fairly and sensibly to resolve the outstanding obligation.
items.title: Singapore Court Orders Car Dealer to Pay Rival $300,000 Despite Ferrari Dispute

items.summary: Volvo Cars announced plans to cut 2,500 jobs globally, with 2,000 positions in Sweden, following a third-quarter adjusted operating loss of 3.7 billion Swedish kronor. The company, majority-owned by Geely Holding, cites tough competition, tariffs, and weak demand as drivers for the cost-reduction strategy aimed at achieving further savings by 2027.
items.title: Volvo Cars Announces 2,500 Job Cuts Amid Q3 Losses

items.summary: Elon Musk reportedly invested approximately $1bn in Skydance, a media empire led by David Ellison following Paramount's merger with Warner Bros Discovery. Semafor first reported the news. The cash infusion solidifies an alliance between two of Trump's richest backers. Skydance co-CEOs warned of layoffs and cost savings targets. A coalition of 12 states previously sued Paramount over competition concerns.
items.title: Elon Musk reportedly invests $1bn in Skydance

items.summary: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor criticized the removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra's exhibition at Bikaner House, calling it a disgrace that damages India's global reputation. Tharoor argued the images depicted events rather than political positions. Vadra alleged management requested the removal, while the venue stated photos did not comply with guidelines. The controversy drew political attention, with Kerala's chief minister offering to host the exhibition fully.
items.title: Shashi Tharoor Criticizes Removal of Raihan Vadra Photos from Exhibition

items.summary: A magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Xizang's Nagqu City on October 23, 2026, killing 16 people and injuring 46, according to the city's emergency management bureau. The tremor damaged 339 houses and affected 20 livestock sheds. Rescue forces, including police, fire services, and military units, have arrived to conduct intensive operations. The China Earthquake Administration initiated a Level-II emergency response, while the region activated a Level-III disaster response. Over 300 police officers and 347 fire personnel are deployed, with relief supplies including tents and clothing arriving. Damage assessments continue as rescue efforts proceed through the night.
items.title: M7.0 Earthquake in Xizang Kills 16, Triggers Major Rescue

items.summary: India has called for urgent reforms to the United Nations Security Council, arguing its 80-year-old structure fails to address global conflicts. Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni stated the Council must reflect present-day realities, noting that 1945 frameworks no longer represent the international community. He highlighted India's contributions and the under-representation of regions like Asia-Pacific, urging the Council to evolve for relevance.
items.title: India Urges UNSC Reform Amidst Calls for Structural Changes

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that the India-US trade deal is in its final stage, noting that negotiations have continued for over a year. He emphasized that the agreement is not complete until finalized, acknowledging challenges remain in the last mile. Jaishankar discussed the deal during a meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai, highlighting bilateral ties strained by US trade policies and immigration restrictions. He also addressed Pakistan-backed terrorism, asserting India will not overlook terror for better relations, and criticized UN double standards on protests globally.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Nears Final Stage, Says Jaishankar

items.summary: China Media Group (CMG) launched a multilingual AI platform for producing short dramas and animated series at the International Audio-Visual Arts Gala in Shanghai on October 18. The platform utilizes large AI models and multilingual resources. Officials announced a joint initiative for audiovisual co-creation, while Shanghai Mayor Zhu Zhongming pledged support for AI-assisted content and next-generation television. The event showcased immersive technologies and digital inclusion initiatives.
items.title: China Media Group Launches Multilingual AI Platform at Shanghai Event

items.summary: A State Council Information Office press conference outlined China's trade and investment progress. Outbound investment reached $128.62 billion in the first nine months of 2026. Free trade zones saw significant growth in imports, exports, and foreign investment. China aims to strengthen goods, services, and digital trade during the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
items.title: China Outlines Trade and Investment Priorities for 2026-2030

items.summary: Simon Richards, head of Insurance Solutions at Insight Investment, stated that China is in a good position to develop its pension framework. Speaking at the 2026 Financial Street Forum, Richards noted that China remains at an early stage in developing its third-pillar pension system. He added that this early stage gives China an opportunity to learn from other countries' experiences.
items.title: Simon Richards Says China Has Opportunity To Develop Pension Framework

items.summary: Karnataka recorded a 35% rainfall deficit between June 1 and September 30, 2026, prompting the state government to launch a 60-day cloud-seeding programme costing around ₹28 crore (₹285 million). Weather experts, including senior IMD officials, caution that conditions are unfavourable due to a lack of rain-bearing clouds and limited public communication. While previous studies in Solapur showed an 18% rainfall enhancement, experts note significant uncertainties. The programme faces scrutiny regarding its viability late in the monsoon and the accuracy of available radar data for identifying suitable clouds.
items.title: Karnataka launches cloud seeding despite expert doubts on drought relief

items.summary: In a podcast episode, economist Tyler Cowen joins Rabbi David Wolpe to discuss artificial intelligence, religion, and human nature. Cowen suggests that AI's primary effect may be on social status, particularly regarding experts like rabbis facing competition from tools like ChatGPT. He further proposes that losing a monopoly on intelligence could paradoxically make humans feel more unique rather than less so.
items.title: Podcast Explores AI's Impact on Human Status and Expertise with Rabbi Wolpe

items.summary: The United Federation of Resident Welfare Associations (UFERWAS) in Hyderabad submitted a representation to Jayesh Ranjan, Special Chief Secretary of MA&UD. The delegation highlighted key issues including strengthening Ward committees under the CURE Act, providing rainwater harvesting pits, improving road infrastructure, and better management of STP water. They urged authorities to take measures to enhance urban governance and citizen participation.
items.title: UFERWAS Urges Jayesh Ranjan to Improve Civic Infrastructure in Hyderabad

items.summary: The New York City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park, with the measure set to take effect in June 2028 if signed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The decision follows years of debate regarding animal welfare and public safety, highlighted by a fatal incident involving a loose horse. While the ban aims to protect public health, it also impacts approximately 150 active carriage drivers, prompting concerns from the Transport Workers Union about worker protections and potential compensation.
items.title: New York City Council Votes to Ban Horse-Drawn Carriages in Central Park

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar alleged that an industrialist wearing Meta smart glasses attempted to secretly record him and Kerala Congress CM VD Satheesan. Shivakumar claimed the visitor, who met him and Satheesan but not other state leaders, shifted the conversation to politics, raising suspicions of a wider sting operation targeting Congress leaders. While Shivakumar stated he has records and knows the individuals involved, he has not disclosed names or evidence. These claims emerge amid a broader controversy over sting-operation videos linked to former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah, involving accusations of conspiracy and demands for independent investigations by opposition parties.
items.title: Karnataka CM Alleges Sting Attempt Using Meta Glasses Amid Political Row

items.summary: Typhoon Champi struck Taiwan, killing one person on Liuqiu island and injuring 94 others. Enormous waves crashed in Keelung, forcing emergency workers to clear debris. Schools, offices, and nearly 1,300 evacuated residents faced closures and evacuations. The storm weakened from 298 km/h to 155 km/h. Over 931 flights were cancelled, leaving stranded passengers at Songshan Airport. The centre moved north toward Japan, where one person was injured and nearly 2,000 homes lost power.
items.title: Typhoon Champi Causes Deadly Chaos and Widespread Disruption Across Taiwan

items.summary: Victoria Beckham has launched her first homeware collection in collaboration with European brand Westwing, themed 'Serving Style'. The range features tableware and textiles inspired by the 19th-century Arts and Crafts movement and her fashion designs. Beckham stated the collaboration explores meaningful moments through design and craftsmanship. The collection is available online and in stores across Germany, France, and Denmark.
items.title: Victoria Beckham Launches Debut Homeware Collection With Westwing

items.summary: Kerala Police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against Eben Paul regarding an arson attack, while Delhi Police restricted traffic in Connaught Place and near Gurudwara Bangla Sahib due to protests. Authorities imposed Section 163 to prohibit gatherings, and the National Investigation Agency is probing a potential wider terror conspiracy extending to Pune.
items.title: Police Act Against Arson Suspect; Delhi Traffic Shut for Protests

items.summary: UK consumer confidence fell at its fastest rate since the 2016 Brexit vote, dropping 11 percentage points to -24 in October, according to GfK. The decline is attributed to rising living costs and the war in the Middle East. This marks the largest single-month drop since July 2016, just before the EU referendum.
items.title: UK Consumer Confidence Plunges as Cost of Living Bites

items.summary: Bangladesh issued a special ordinance to accelerate distributed solar deployment on government buildings, addressing regulatory gaps in tariffs and maintenance. The measure facilitates private-sector investment through Opex and Capex models, aiming to support a target of adding 3 GW to 4 GW of renewable capacity. While investors welcome the move, they call for further measures to address remaining barriers and ensure transparent participation.
items.title: Bangladesh issues ordinance to accelerate rooftop solar investment

items.summary: A YouTube program examines whether the Modi government is yielding to US pressure regarding oil, trade, and agriculture. The analysis cites reduced Russian oil purchases, a visit by Rubio, and a photo involving Hardeep Singh Puri and Jeffrey Epstein as evidence of shifting power dynamics in US-India relations. The episode questions New Delhi's ability to resist Washington's demands.
items.title: Analysis Questions If Modi Government Is Yielding To Trump Pressure

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police issued a traffic advisory for a protest march by a left-wing organisation from Bangla Sahib Gurudwara to Jantar Mantar on Friday. Traffic diversions will remain in effect from 1pm to 5pm, covering areas including Connaught Place and Parliament Street. Commuters are urged to avoid unnecessary travel, use alternative routes, and follow traffic instructions to ensure smooth movement during the specified period.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Issues Advisory for Left-Wing Protest March

items.summary: Jio Platforms' US$3.2 billion IPO attracted record demand on its final day, with total subscriptions exceeding US$16 billion. The offering, valued at up to US$108.3 billion, saw retail and employee quotas oversubscribed significantly. Anchor investors including BlackRock and Fidelity participated, while the listing is expected to begin on Oct 28.
items.title: Jio Platforms IPO Sees Record Bids on Final Day

items.summary: Japan's inflation rate exceeded 2% for the first time this year, reaching 2.1% in September according to government data. Core inflation, excluding volatile food prices, also hit 2.1%, while the rate excluding both food and energy climbed to 2.4%. The increase intensifies pressure on the central bank to maintain vigilance and consider raising interest rates to combat rising prices.
items.title: Japan Inflation Tops 2% Target Amid Rising Prices

items.summary: The State Bank of India (SBI) warns customers against searching online for bank customer care numbers, as fraudsters use fake listings to trick people into sharing sensitive details or transferring money. SBI advises obtaining support details only from the official website. This advisory is part of its National Cyber Security Month Special Campaign 6.0, promoting safe digital banking practices and helping people recognize online scams.
items.title: SBI Warns Customers Against Searching for Fake Bank Helpline Numbers Online

items.summary: Indian para-shooter Mona Agarwal set a new world record of 357.5 in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 event at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. She also broke the Asian record of 355.7. Agarwal, who won bronze in Paris 2024, secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota in this competition.
items.title: Mona Agarwal Shatters World Record at Asian Para Games

items.summary: Researchers from Melanoma Institute Australia report a world-first cancer vaccine significantly reduces the risk of melanoma recurrence and death. The phase 3 trial, involving 1,137 patients across 157 global sites, found a 42 per cent reduction in recurrence risk when the personalised mRNA-based vaccine was combined with pembrolizumab immunotherapy. Principal investigator Georgina Long described the results as transformational and better than expected. While the treatment targets high-risk patients with advanced melanoma, experts note it is not preventative and does not work for all patients. Regulatory review is ongoing, with results set for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine.
items.title: Australian-led trial shows breakthrough cancer vaccine reduces melanoma recurrence risk

items.summary: Officials in Yamanashi Prefecture held a tabletop drill to plan evacuating thousands of foreign tourists if Mount Fuji erupts. The exercise examined using boats and buses, addressing language barriers, and coordinating with embassies to ensure safe departure.
items.title: Officials in Yamanashi Plan Evacuation for Tourists If Mount Fuji Erupts

items.summary: Fifteen Indigenous youth are set to begin a landmark trial in October 2026 against Canada and its attorney general, alleging that the government's net-zero emissions plan infringes on their Charter rights to life, liberty, and security. Leandrea Taylor Reeves, a plaintiff from the Yukon, will testify on how climate change disrupts cultural practices and endangers her community. The case, the first federal youth-led climate trial in Canadian history, seeks to enforce a science-based emissions trajectory. While the government maintains its commitment to net-zero goals, the plaintiffs argue current policies prioritize fossil fuels over Indigenous rights and safety.
items.title: Indigenous Youth Launch Landmark Climate Trial Against Canada

items.summary: Prof Devi Sridhar questions the reliability of an AI model developed by Mass General Brigham researchers to predict cancer survival using facial images. While the FAHR-FaceSurvival model showed associations in 18 of 28 cancer categories, Sridhar notes it is not conclusive and may exhibit racial bias, particularly for Black patients. She highlights that the tool relies on retrospective data and is significantly affected by lighting, cosmetic procedures, and facial expressions. Sridhar argues that while the research is promising, the jump from statistical associations to accurate clinical prediction remains uncertain, and the model's utility in daily practice is yet to be proven.
items.title: Devi Sridhar Questions AI's Ability to Predict Cancer Survival from Selfies

items.summary: The Indian government has imposed a price cap on 137 cancer drugs following a Supreme Court ruling that described industry mark-ups as extortion. The decision follows a legal case brought by Sarojam Radhakrishnan, who could not afford her treatment. Analysis by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority revealed trade mark-ups averaging 170%, with some reaching over 700%. Officials state the measure could reduce prices by up to 70% and save 2,500 crore rupees annually. However, civil society groups warn that a total overhaul of the healthcare supply chain is needed to prevent companies from finding legal loopholes or raising other charges.
items.title: India caps cancer drug prices after court calls mark-ups extortion

items.summary: Reuters reports that the Japanese government may reduce gasoline subsidies starting in December due to unsustainable costs. Subsidies, introduced in March to keep prices near $1.09 per liter, now cost billions monthly. Plans could raise the average price to $1.11 in December and $1.15 in January. Officials aim to offset this with a food tax cut beginning in April.
items.title: Japan Considers Cutting Gasoline Subsidies Amid Rising Energy Costs

items.summary: Enel Colombia has commenced commercial operations at its 256 MW Atlántico solar plant in northern Colombia, completing a three-plant complex with approximately 985 MW total capacity. The facility, located between Sabanalarga and Usiacurí, features 403,920 solar modules across 34 arrays and spans 415 hectares. Enel stated the project created over 2,500 jobs, with local residents accounting for more than 75% of the workforce.
items.title: Enel Colombia Commences Operations at 256 MW Atlántico Solar Plant

items.summary: A morning briefing on October 23, 2026, highlights US President Donald Trump suggesting Washington may carry out further strikes on Iran, stating the US had already dealt significant damage. Simultaneously, a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Tibet's Nagqu City killed at least 16 people and injured 54, prompting a national emergency response upgrade. In diplomatic news, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hosted R4 and E3 meetings in Istanbul to address regional issues including the Palestinian question and the Russia-Ukraine war. Additionally, France remains on maximum vigilance ahead of demonstrations on October 24, with security deployments expected to increase by 20%.
items.title: Trump Suggests Further Iran Strikes Amid Global News Briefing

items.summary: ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Kapur confirmed ongoing face-offs with Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh, stating the situation continues after incidents began in July. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence on the border issue. While the government denied new Chinese occupation, Union Minister Kiren Rijiju acknowledged local concerns regarding grazing access.
items.title: ITBP DG Confirms Ongoing India-China Face-offs in Arunachal Pradesh

items.summary: Greens senator Jordon Steele-John remains in limbo following allegations of inappropriate behavior toward women. New leader David Shoebridge faces pressure to investigate, while Steele-John denies wrongdoing and accuses internal factions of political games. The party must decide whether to allow Steele-John to attend Senate estimates or force his leave, a move requiring two-thirds support. The situation highlights tensions between leadership, party processes, and public optics regarding misconduct allegations.
items.title: Greens Leader Faces Challenge Over Senator Steele-John Allegations

items.summary: On International Snow Leopard Day, reporting highlights how science and community efforts aid coexistence. A 2025 survey found roughly 397 snow leopards in Nepal. Research shows predators coexist by targeting different prey. Experts warn that wild prey decline drives attacks on livestock. Initiatives like the Ak Ilbirs corridor aim to adapt habitats to climate change while supporting local herders.
items.title: Science and Community Action Foster Snow Leopard Coexistence

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspended licences for eight eateries in Mumbai and seized nearly 38 tonnes of food stock across the state. Inspections revealed violations such as unhygienic kitchens and the use of unauthorized food colours. Officials did not specify which violations occurred at each establishment, though the largest seizure involved kidney beans in Navi Mumbai.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA suspends eight Mumbai eateries and seizes food stock

items.summary: Debretsion Gebremichael, leader of Ethiopia's Tigray People's Liberation Front, stated on Tigrayan television that the northern state remains at war with federal forces. He claimed tactical victories and alleged the neutralization of hundreds of soldiers. Conversely, the army recaptured Mekelle after TPLF withdrawal. Analysts warn the advance may escalate conflict with Eritrea, while recent strikes have killed civilians in Tigray and Amhara regions.
items.title: TPLF Leader Claims War Continues in Tigray Despite Army Advances

items.summary: Conflicting reports have emerged regarding restrictions on Ukraine's access to the Starshield satellite system. While US President Donald Trump stated that access was restored and blamed no one, a senior European official reported that speed limits remain in place at approximately 100mph. Trump administration officials, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, denied ordering the throttling, shifting responsibility to Elon Musk's private company. Conversely, Musk asserted that US government decisions control Starshield limits. Ukrainian President Zelensky confirmed ongoing speed restrictions in some areas and expressed frustration over the lack of a clear explanation for the interruptions affecting military communications.
items.title: US Officials and Elon Musk Clash Over Ukraine Starshield Restrictions

items.summary: Rising inflation and fuel prices are forcing pensioners to drastically cut household costs. Errol McGuiness, 79, lives in the dark to save on electricity, while Bryan, 83, restricts his living space. Melissa Baydilly of Affordable Foods notes that price hikes of 25% to 30% are common, leaving many seniors unable to afford essentials like fruit and vegetables.
items.title: Rising Bills Force Pensioners to Cut Costs and Live in Darkness

items.summary: Brent crude prices rose to $114.00 per barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including Aramco facilities, raised concerns over oil flows. ING analysts noted markets fear renewed escalation in the Persian Gulf. Consequently, the bank revised its fourth-quarter Brent outlook, deeming a previously estimated $80 average unattainable.
items.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Infrastructure Drive Oil Prices Higher

items.summary: The India Fix newsletter examines the Special Intensive Revision of India's voter rolls, noting that the exercise has deleted 13 crore voters from draft lists. While the BJP cites undocumented migrants from Bangladesh as the reason, the article highlights that Bangladesh's per capita GDP in 2026 is marginally higher than India's. The newsletter compares this to Assam's 2019 National Register of Citizens exercise, where 1.9 million were excluded despite claims of over six million undocumented migrants. The author argues the rhetoric targets India's Muslim citizens rather than actual migrants, suggesting the revision benefits the BJP by excluding opponents' voters.
items.title: Newsletter Analyzes BJP Voter Roll Revision Amid Bangladesh GDP Comparison

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is meeting with student representatives and law enforcement to address ongoing student protests over teacher shortages and school conditions. He is also holding a defence council to prepare for planned demonstrations. Authorities in Lyon and Marseille have banned Saturday's protests, while Macron stated that demonstrations not organized by workers' unions would be banned. A court suspended a Paris police order banning a university student march, which saw hundreds of participants.
items.title: Macron Meets Student Representatives and Law Enforcement Ahead of Protests

items.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Nigeria and Kenya may have crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe airport on 3 October. While both patients passed through the airport on the same day, no link has been established regarding shared equipment or contact. The Nigerian patient, a 42-year-old woman, is showing signs of improvement, while the Kenyan patient has died. Authorities are examining possible common sources and conducting genomic sequencing. Officials emphasize that the source of exposure remains unknown and urge vigilance without panic, noting the difficulty of screening at porous borders.
items.title: Nigeria and Kenya Ebola patients may have crossed paths at Uganda airport, officials say

items.summary: The World Health Organization's Africa chief warned that the continent faces a complex Ebola outbreak after the virus spread from east Africa to Nigeria. Nigeria confirmed an imported Bundibugyo strain case in a diplomat with travel history to Uganda. This marks the fourth African nation affected, reigniting memories of the 2014 outbreak that killed over 11,000 people in west Africa.
items.title: WHO warns Africa faces complex Ebola outbreak after Nigeria reports first case

items.summary: The article recommends two free online tools, vidshift.io and nanofile.io, for compressing files without uploading them to untrustworthy servers. Both tools are provided by the same developer and are designed to reduce file sizes for videos and other documents. The service allows users to start uploading and compressing files in about a minute, though actual compression times vary based on file size. This tip originally appeared in The Intelligence's Cool Tools newsletter.
items.title: Two Free Online Tools Offer Privacy-Focused File Compression

items.summary: eMudhra shares fell 40% over three sessions following a security incident involving its global SSL/TLS certificate business. Chairman V. Srinivasan stated the company revoked affected certificate authorities within 14 hours and confirmed no data breach or infrastructure compromise. The board decided to exit the segment, which contributes about 1% of global revenue, citing rising compliance costs and reduced business potential due to free alternatives. An independent researcher identified weak keys in the company's Key Generation Ceremony, prompting an investigation. The company is issuing replacement certificates to affected customers.
items.title: eMudhra Exits SSL Business After Security Incident

items.summary: Infosys announced a dividend of Rs 26 per share, payable on November 11 to shareholders holding demat accounts as of November 3. The IT major reported a 6% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,823 crore for the July-September quarter, alongside an 11% increase in revenue from operations to Rs 49,244 crore.
items.title: Infosys Announces Dividend and Reports Strong Q2 Profit Growth

items.summary: Apple launched its foldable iPhone Duo on Friday, reviving scenes of overnight lines and intense demand despite limited supply. The device, priced from $2,000 up to $3,199 for high-storage models, marks a major design shift in the company's nearly two-decade history. While crowds gathered in cities like Beijing and Singapore, many buyers were existing Apple customers eager for innovation. However, production challenges involving advanced hinges and display technology, along with component shortages, have constrained availability. Consequently, new orders face delivery delays extending into late January or even December, marking some of the longest waits for a new Apple product in recent years.
items.title: Apple launches foldable iPhone Duo amid supply shortages and high demand

items.summary: Tata Motors Ltd reported a net profit of ₹2,138 crore in the September quarter, marking a return to standalone profitability after a previous loss. Standalone revenue jumped 41.9% to ₹23,930 crore, driven by higher commercial vehicle volumes. Managing Director Girish Wagh highlighted strong underlying demand and disciplined execution. The company also noted steady progress in its Iveco acquisition, with consolidation expected from the December quarter.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Profit Rebound and Iveco Acquisition Progress

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre in Jatni, Odisha, on October 25. Officials stated the facility, spanning 18.55 acres, will enhance cybersecurity and disaster recovery. BJP leader Jatin Mohanty noted this marks the PM's ninth visit to the state since 2024, aiming to boost digital infrastructure and electronics manufacturing.
items.title: PM Modi to Inaugure RBI Data Centre in Odisha

items.summary: Infosys reduced its fiscal year 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1-2%, down from 1.5-3%, despite reporting a 10.7% quarterly revenue increase. The company cited AI-driven shifts in client demand and pricing pressures as key factors. While the energy segment grew 7.3%, overall revenue rose only 1.5% excluding currency effects. Net profit increased 6.2% but missed analyst expectations.
items.title: Infosys Lowers FY27 Revenue Growth Forecast Amid AI Challenges

items.summary: Infosys Ltd reported a 6.23 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,823 crore for the second quarter of FY27. Revenue from operations rose 10.7 per cent to Rs 49,244 crore. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 1.5 per cent year-on-year and 1.2 per cent quarter-on-quarter.
items.title: Infosys Reports Profit Rise and Revenue Growth in Q2 FY27

items.summary: Tata Motors Limited announced a consolidated net profit of ₹1,257 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, a substantial increase from ₹530 crore in the previous year. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 36% to ₹25,338 crore, while profit before tax turned positive at ₹1,998 crore after a loss in the prior period. MD & CEO Girish Wagh attributed the growth to broad-based performance across segments.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Strong Q2 FY27 Earnings and Profit Growth

items.summary: Tata Motors Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1,257 crore for Q2 FY27, a 50.90% decline from Q1 but a recovery from a loss last year. Revenue rose 36%, though the headline profit was impacted by lower mark-to-market losses on Tata Capital investments.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Q2 Net Profit Amid Revenue Growth

items.summary: Infosys reduced its fiscal year 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1-2 percent, down from 1.5-3 percent, despite beating quarterly estimates. The company cited increased demand from energy and utility clients. However, the broader IT sector faces headwinds from AI, which is shifting client focus toward productivity gains rather than traditional billing models. Infosys shares remained flat ahead of results.
items.title: Infosys Lowers Revenue Growth Forecast Amid AI Industry Challenges

items.summary: Lionel Messi requested a chess opening tailored to his playing style from the AI chatbot ChatGPT, a video of the interaction that went viral on social media. The AI suggested the opening known as 'Goat Horns,' consisting of the moves 1.e4 a6 2.d4 c6. Chess.com noted that AI models often provide poor chess advice and that top professionals are unlikely to approve this specific opening. The video was captioned by ChatGPT, stating it suggested 'Goat Horns.' This incident occurred shortly after OpenAI released an updated interface for visual and interactive responses.
items.title: Messi Asks ChatGPT for a Chess Opening Matched to His Style

items.summary: Tata Group-owned retailer Westside introduced a fixed Rs 49 fee for all credit card transactions starting October 8, 2026. The company did not specify the reason for the charge, though it noted processing costs like MDR often drive such fees. The Reserve Bank of India has not issued specific instructions on credit card surcharges, distinguishing them from debit card rules. Customers are advised to check bills before payment.
items.title: Westside Introduces Rs 49 Credit Card Fee Amid RBI Silence

items.summary: Microsoft is shutting down The Garage, a 17-year-old program that provided maker spaces and tools for employee side projects across 15 regions. CEO Satya Nadella participated in its hackathons, which produced products like Seeing AI and the Xbox Adaptive Controller. While the program ends, Microsoft states experimentation will continue within daily team workflows, though specific impacts on locations and employees remain unclear.
items.title: Microsoft Closes The Garage Maker Lab Program

items.summary: Tesla announced a financing offer for the Model Y in India on October 23, featuring a monthly payment of Rs 39,990 under a seven-year step-up EMI plan at 8.5% interest. The company claims an effective cost of Rs 19,990 by deducting estimated fuel and maintenance savings, though this figure is not the actual loan instalment. The promotion runs during the Switch and Save Carnival at experience centres across major Indian cities.
items.title: Tesla Launches Model Y Financing Offer in India

items.summary: A former Justice Department official told Semafor that a Tesla-SpaceX merger could face real antitrust risks due to potential vertical foreclosure. Sen. Cory Booker stated that if Elon Musk proceeds, the deal would carry risks for global antitrust enforcers. Additionally, Reuters reported that Tesla's work in China and its relationship with the Pentagon could complicate matters, while Democrats might scrutinize the deal if they regain control of the House.
items.title: Elon Musk's Potential Tesla-SpaceX Merger Faces Antitrust Scrutiny

items.summary: This week's VoxDev newsletter highlights diverse development economics research. Topics include a new framework for scaling education interventions, GPS apps reshaping tractor rental markets in Kenya, and job search mismatches in Addis Ababa. Studies also examine tax collection efficiency, showing low-income countries collect significantly less per dollar spent than high-income nations, and find no gender discrimination in Ethiopian loan decisions.
items.title: VoxDev Weekly Highlights Research on Education, Agriculture, and Tax Efficiency

items.summary: Jensen Huang stated there is a scarcity of capital for the AI buildout, noting demand exceeds availability. This comment follows a selloff where S&P 500 futures fell 0.28% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.6%. CoreWeave stock declined 10%, while Nvidia and Alphabet shares also fell. CNBC reports the selloff highlights worries that financing, rather than demand, could limit the AI rally.
items.title: Jensen Huang warns of AI capital scarcity amid market drops

items.summary: Luxury brands like Hermes and Cartier face steeper slumps in mainland China as wealthy consumers reduce spending. Sales for major labels fell by double digits in August and September, according to research firms. While resilient demand in Hong Kong and Macau offset some mainland declines, earnings remain weighed down. Executives fear the slump could persist until 2027 due to scrutiny of offshore wealth and a cooling AI stock rally. Consumers are shifting toward experiences and understated products, signaling a structural problem rather than a temporary dip.
items.title: Wealthy Chinese Consumers Cut Back on Luxury Spending

items.summary: Singapore Exchange CEO Loh Boon Chye announced he will step down in 2027. He cited the bourse's strong performance and foundation as the opportunity to plan a thoughtful leadership transition. Chairman Koh Boon Hwee described the decision as bittersweet, crediting Loh with stabilizing the company and transforming it into a global multi-asset platform.
items.title: SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye to step down in 2027

items.summary: Xiongan New Area in Hebei Province is developing as a model smart city by integrating digital and physical infrastructure. The Xiongan Urban Computing Center acts as the digital brain, supporting over 100 data categories from 20 government departments. AI applications optimize traffic flow, reducing peak travel times by 15 minutes in Rongdong District, while smart systems monitor utilities and detect safety hazards. The city has built more than 500 kilometers of digital roads and over 130 kilometers of digital utility tunnels. By 2027, Xiongan aims to attract five unicorn companies and 100 leading enterprises to foster innovation and talent development.
items.title: Xiongan New Area Deploys AI and Digital Infrastructure for Smart City Vision

items.summary: Raj Thackeray of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena accused the BJP of murdering democracy, alleging the party used religious polarisation to divert attention from a viral audio clip. Thackeray claimed the recording featured BJP and RSS officials discussing strategies to silence activist Manoj Jarange regarding a Rs 500 crore payment. While Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered a forensic examination, BJP leaders questioned the clip's authenticity and suggested it might be AI-generated.
items.title: Raj Thackeray Accuses BJP of Democracy Murder Over Audio Clip

items.summary: Delhi Police detained protesters attempting to march to the Election Commission headquarters against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Authorities imposed prohibitory orders banning mass gatherings. The demonstration, organized by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, drew students, youth, and activists. Organizers stated the protest would remain peaceful. Security was tightened in central Delhi with traffic diversions in place.
items.title: Protesters Detained as March Against Electoral Roll Revision Heads to Election Commission

items.summary: China Media Group (CMG) launched a multilingual AI production platform for short dramas and animated series at the International Audio-Visual Arts Gala in Shanghai on October 18. The event, held at the Shanghai Exhibition Center, showcased projects combining technology and art. CMG officials and Shanghai Mayor Zhu Zhongming addressed the gathering, pledging deeper cooperation to support cultural innovation through technology and promote international exchanges.
items.title: China Media Group Launches Multilingual AI Platform at Shanghai Event

items.summary: The 2026 'China Walk: Vibrant Hainan' joint media tour launched in Sanya on October 19, bringing together journalists from 11 outlets across eight ASEAN countries. Hosted by China Media Group and the Hainan Bureau, the event explores rural revitalization and development within the Hainan Free Trade Port through on-site reporting and multimedia content distribution.
items.title: China Walk Media Tour Launches in Hainan for ASEAN Journalists

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping recalled the 'Half a Quilt' story during a gathering commemorating the 90th anniversary of the Long March victory. He emphasized that remembering history is crucial for creating a brighter future and stressed the importance of people's support. The article notes that Shazhou Village, where the story originated, has seen significant improvements in livelihoods and income since 2012, reflecting the Party's commitment to modernization and shared prosperity.
items.title: Xi Jinping Recalls 'Half a Quilt' Story at Long March Anniversary

items.summary: A commentary highlights an 81% global decline in migratory freshwater fish since the 1970s, driven by habitat fragmentation and dams. While a 2026 disaster in Nepal demonstrated the fragility of infrastructure and the ecological disruption of sediment floods, the author argues that top-down engineering often fails. Instead, the piece points to successful community-led conservation in Meghalaya, Bhutan, and Nagaland. These grassroots models protect spawning grounds without concrete, offering a viable alternative to restore river biodiversity and support local livelihoods.
items.title: Community Models Offer Hope for Disappearing Migratory Fish

items.summary: The nuclear industry faces a critical leadership challenge as it prepares for a projected four million professionals by 2050. Success depends not just on technical skills but on leaders who can navigate complex international systems, manage diverse supply chains, and foster safety cultures. The World Nuclear University Summer Institute addresses this by training mid-career professionals in global contexts, such as the 2027 program in Cape Town. With over 1,700 alumni from 90 countries, the initiative builds networks essential for managing new builds and extending existing fleets. Applications for the 2027 cohort close on 27 November 2026.
items.title: Nuclear Industry Leaders Need Global Skills for Future Growth

items.summary: Cockroach Janata Party leaders appeared in court regarding bail conditions and trespassing charges. Simultaneously, a strike by 40,000 Haryana electricity workers caused power outages affecting 50,000 households. The Haryana Power Minister opposes privatization and plans to challenge the regulatory commission's order. Leaders face summons from the Delhi Police Crime Branch regarding ongoing investigations.
items.title: Cockroach Janata Party Leaders Face Legal Scrutiny Amid Power Strike

items.summary: Police in a Parisian suburb are treating a shooting as a terrorist incident. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that one person was killed and at least four others injured in Trappes. The National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office has taken over the investigation. Reports suggest the number of injured may be higher, potentially including a 12-year-old child. The Mayor of Trappes reported that an individual fired shots from a vehicle at several people.
items.title: One Dead, Four Injured in Paris Suburb Shooting Treated as Terrorist Incident

items.summary: Greece's renewable electricity capacity is approaching 20 GW, driven by significant additions in wind and photovoltaic projects. Despite high curtailments and low wholesale prices impacting profitability, the sector continues to expand. The Independent Power Transmission Operator expects installations to reach nearly 20 GW by year-end, while the Ministry of Environment and Energy aims for 4 GW of storage by 2028. Industry groups highlight concerns over market distortions and investment delays.
items.title: Greece Renewable Capacity Growth Amid Market Challenges

items.summary: Approximately 40,000 Haryana electricity employees launched a three-day strike in Gurugram and Nuh, protesting a regulatory decision to grant a parallel power distribution licence to a private firm. The action triggered massive outages affecting over 50,000 households and 1,800 manufacturing units, causing severe water shortages and business disruptions. The state government opposes privatisation and plans to legally challenge the order.
items.title: Electricity Workers Strike in Haryana Causes Widespread Power Outages

items.summary: Oil prices reached a five-month high amid fears of renewed US military strikes on Iran. Brent crude rose 1% to $114.72 a barrel. Analysts note that reports of potential attacks, rather than a brief conflict, have driven market volatility. Tensions remain high as Iran threatens retaliation against Gulf facilities and US forces consider action following elections.
items.title: Oil Prices Surge on Fears of Renewed US Strikes on Iran

items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned the UK could face a winter of greater flooding. Speaking at a wildfire summit, he emphasized the need for resilience as unexpected events become more common. He also addressed supply preparedness and upcoming storms.
items.title: Andy Burnham Warns UK Faces Winter Flooding Risks Amid Climate Concerns

items.summary: Mississippi officials lowered a 31-ton propane tank and steel tower into the Gulf to create an artificial reef. Supported by Chevron and local fire departments, the structures aim to provide shelter for fish in areas with limited natural habitats. While a 2023 reef supported over 530 red snapper, no figures exist yet for this new deployment. The project is expected to benefit both commercial and recreational fishing.
items.title: Mississippi Deploys Retired Firefighting Equipment as Artificial Reef

items.summary: Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu appointed Asian Para Games gold medallist Suvarna Raj as the State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities. Officials stated she was selected from a panel of three candidates recommended by a committee. Raj, a discus throw champion and disability rights advocate, will oversee safeguards for persons with disabilities under the law.
items.title: Asian Para Games gold medallist Suvarna Raj appointed Delhi disability commissioner

items.summary: Doctors told the BBC that paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during a siege in Darfur a year ago. A BBC investigation found evidence supporting these claims of targeting. UN human rights chief Volker Türk described the findings as deeply disturbing, noting that attacking health facilities is illegal under international law. However, Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud, the health minister of the group's civilian-affiliated government, dismissed the allegations as propaganda.
items.title: Doctors Report Paramilitary Targeting of Sudanese Hospitals in Darfur

items.summary: Facing prohibitive new car prices averaging over $50,000 and monthly payments exceeding $765, many young Americans are increasingly purchasing older Y2K-era vehicles. Jack Price, a Marine veteran, exemplifies this trend by driving a 2010 Volkswagen Jetta he bought for $6,000, noting the financial relief of avoiding a car payment. While experts like Keith Barry caution that older cars may lack modern safety features and suffer from reliability issues, buyers cite the ability to perform DIY repairs and the lower total cost of ownership as primary attractions. Despite the shrinking inventory of affordable used vehicles, the movement persists as a response to economic strain, with some owners embracing the mechanical challenges as part of the vehicle's appeal.
items.title: Young Americans Turn to Y2K Cars Amidst Rising Vehicle Costs

items.summary: The Japanese government highlighted the urgent need to strengthen its energy supply-and-demand structure in the fiscal 2025 white paper, adopted at a Cabinet meeting. The document notes Japan was the first to release petroleum reserves due to the Middle East situation. It also outlines plans to secure fossil fuel supplies while accelerating nuclear and renewable energy use.
items.title: Japan Calls for Stronger Energy Supply Structure in Fiscal 2025 White Paper

items.summary: Delhi authorities seized over 322 kg of ghee from stores offering steep discounts ahead of the festive season. Inspections targeted retailers promoting deals like 'Buy One, Get One Free' and discounts up to 60 per cent. Officials collected samples from locations including Vikaspuri and Hastal village to assess quality and prevent the sale of adulterated products. Further action will follow laboratory test reports.
items.title: Delhi Seizes Hundreds of Kilograms of Ghee Amidst Discount Checks

items.summary: An explosion at a privately owned coal mine in Gelik, Turkey, killed two miners and injured five others, with one person still trapped. Local authorities attributed the blast to firedamp. Zonguldak governor Osman Hacibektasoglu confirmed two deaths after hospitalization. Rescue teams from AFAD and medical crews responded to the site. An investigation has been opened to determine the exact cause of the incident.
items.title: Explosion at Turkish Coal Mine Kills Two, Traps One

items.summary: South Africa has proposed a new fiscal law designed to protect public finances from future populist governments, coinciding with a projected decline in debt for the first time in nearly two decades. Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana introduced the measure to lock in gains, noting that debt stabilized at around $366 billion, or 78% of GDP, after rising from 24% in 2009. Unlike other nations, the draft law lacks a specific numerical ceiling, instead requiring future administrations to explain deviations from their announced plans. While economists view the numbers as warranting a credit rating upgrade, critics argue the approach relies on an optimistic premise that political explanations will suffice to maintain fiscal discipline.
items.title: South Africa Proposes New Fiscal Law to Shield Public Finances

items.summary: Delhi Police detained protesters marching against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls on Friday, October 23. Organized by People Against SIR, the demonstration invoked Section 163 of the BNSS to bar mass gatherings. Participants, including leaders from CPI(M) and AIDWA, shouted slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The collective plans further protests in 88 cities across 18 states.
items.title: Delhi Police Detain Protesters During Anti-SIR March

items.summary: Military reinforcements are moving to the Middle East as the U.S. and Israel prepare for a possible attack on Iran following the midterm elections, according to a person briefed on war planning. Iran has stated it is prepared for both diplomacy and war, demanding formal control over the Strait of Hormuz and the withdrawal of U.S. troops. Meanwhile, millions of Americans have already voted early, with Democrats voting at higher rates than Republicans in key battleground states, though experts caution against overinterpreting early data as a predictor of final results.
items.title: Military Reinforcements Move to Mideast as U.S. Prepares for Possible Iran Attack

items.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez held a press conference to announce security arrangements for upcoming protests. He stated that 70,000 security forces would be mobilized on October 24 to maintain order during the events.
items.title: French Interior Minister Announces Security Mobilization for Upcoming Protests

items.summary: A new study analyzed over one million resolved contracts across four platforms, including Polymarket and Kalshi, covering twelve domains. The research found that forecast probabilities were highly calibrated, with events occurring approximately as predicted. While systematic tendencies toward over- or underestimation exist in highly consequential areas, large-scale aggregation of judgments provides meaningful information about real-world uncertainty.
items.title: New Analysis Confirms High Accuracy of Prediction Markets Across Diverse Domains

items.summary: Gary Huang Kunjie was sentenced to 28 weeks in jail for filming upskirt videos of women in June 2026. The court warned him he could face caning if he reoffends. Huang admitted to recording around 20 victims between May and June 2026. He has a history of similar convictions from 2018 to 2025. Judge Arvindren expressed concern Huang might continue reoffending despite his remorse.
items.title: Serial voyeur jailed again for upskirt videos in Singapore

items.summary: Max Doppelt flew to Shanghai to obtain a lung cancer drug approved in China but not the US, noting his mother has survived three years on it. He reports at least 30 Americans have made similar trips. Doppelt argues this highlights a need for FDA reform, citing a proposal by Reps. John Moolenaar and Debbie Dingell to require Treasury clearance for pharmaceutical deals with Chinese companies.
items.title: Max Doppelt Urges FDA Reform After Flying to China for Cancer Drug

items.summary: Two Indigenous women in Brazil were denied interpreter assistance while voting in Macapá, despite their inability to speak Portuguese. Their community leader, Mitore Tiriyó Kaxuyana, reported that poll workers restricted translator access to voters with disabilities only. The women left unsure if their votes were counted correctly. This incident reflects broader concerns about Indigenous voting rights and language access in Brazil's electoral system.
items.title: Indigenous Women Denied Interpreter Assistance During Brazil Election

items.summary: More than four million Latinos have turned 18 since the 2022 midterm elections and will vote for the first time on November 3. This new generation, alongside one million naturalized citizens, brings the total number of new eligible Latino voters to 5.2 million compared to four years ago. Hispanics now account for 16% of all voting-age citizens. The median age of eligible Hispanic voters is 39, significantly younger than other groups. Many new voters cite concerns over immigration policy, ICE operations, and the economy as primary motivations for their participation in the upcoming election.
items.title: Millions of Young Latinos Set to Vote for First Time in Midterms

items.summary: Global equity funds attracted $28.16 billion in net inflows during the week through October 21, marking a fifth consecutive week of positive capital flow. LSEG Lipper data attributes this trend to easing Treasury yields and strong corporate earnings, which lifted investor sentiment across Asian, European, and US markets.
items.title: Global Equity Funds See Fifth Consecutive Week of Inflows

items.summary: Meghan Markle stated she was informed of disturbing allegations against her father in 2018, leading her to limit his contact with their children. Thomas Markle denied possessing alleged child sexual abuse material found in the Philippines. Meghan cited a 2018 letter to police and expressed hope for justice and child safety.
items.title: Meghan Markle Reveals 2018 Warning About Father's Allegations

items.summary: Meta is introducing fees for posting hyperlinks on Facebook, limiting free posts to two per month while charging $49.99 for eight links and $499 for unlimited access. This move follows similar restrictions on Instagram and X. Meanwhile, Oracle faces scrutiny over its $300 billion deal with OpenAI amid $169 billion in debt, as AI efficiency gains challenge the viability of massive data center investments. Separately, utilities may pass grid upgrade costs to consumers even if speculative data centers are never built, and the Trump administration authorized a release of 315,000 barrels of heating oil reserves to potentially lower prices.
items.title: Meta Charges for Hyperlinks as Tech Giants Face Debt and Data Center Uncertainty

items.summary: The Japan Times and News2u Holdings warn partners and former employees that unauthorized access to a server used until August 2022 may have exposed business and personal data, including MyNumber details, though digital services remain unaffected.
items.title: Japan Times and News2u Warn Partners of Potential Data Exposure

items.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu faces a challenging re-election campaign three years after the October 7 Hamas attack, which killed over 1,200 people and took 250 hostages. While Likud holds a parliamentary majority, polls show the party's worst performance since 2006, with support hovering around 19 to 20 seats. Analysts note Netanyahu's weakened position compared to potential winner Gadi Eisenkot, yet he leverages the ongoing conflict and opposition to Arab parties to maintain a realistic chance of power. His strategy involves portraying himself as the only leader capable of finishing the war against Iran, a narrative reinforced by U.S. President Donald Trump.
items.title: Netanyahu Stakes Re-election on War Promise Amid Poll Decline

items.summary: Rohini Mokashi-Punekar reviews Luke Kennard's 2026 Booker-shortlisted novel, Black Bag, which explores enforced anonymity through a professor's experiment based on Robert Zajonc's mere-exposure effect. The unnamed narrator, an out-of-work actor, is zipped into a black leather bag and forced to remain characterless. While the novel contrasts this concealment with Claudio's hyper-visibility and critiques Internet commodification, the reviewer finds the plot insubstantial and the middle stodgy. Although the book features striking, disparate moments, it fails to fully examine contemporary anxieties, leaving the reader feeling cheated of an epiphany. The review concludes that the novel suffers from an uninspired close despite its adventurous chase sequence.
items.title: Review of Luke Kennard's Novel Black Bag

items.summary: Kerala Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob urged the Centre to extend the deadline for activating ration cards via e-KYC. He requested flexibility in implementing the 2025 amendment order affecting over 44,000 priority cardholders who have not purchased supplies for six months. Jacob argued that immediate removal could be unjust and proposed retaining cards under a state category until eligibility is reassessed.
items.title: Kerala Minister Urges Centre to Extend Ration Card e-KYC Deadline

items.summary: An article originally published on the Vanishing Gradients Substack outlines a framework for agentic software factories, designed to allow autonomous and asynchronous execution of software tasks. The authors propose a four-layer hierarchy: harness, personalization, automation, and continual learning. This structure enables agents to build and operate software independently, reducing the need for constant human oversight. The framework emphasizes specification and verification to ensure reliability. Examples include an invoice tracker and a media business setup, demonstrating how agents can handle repetitive tasks, perform checks, and improve over time without retraining. The authors argue this approach empowers non-engineers to direct software development by delegating implementation while retaining control over decisions and trade-offs.
items.title: Authors Propose Agentic Software Factory Hierarchy of Needs

items.summary: The government is expected to raise the earnings limit for its new first-time buyer loan scheme to £110,000 outside London and £140,000 in the capital. These changes, reported by The Times, aim to include middle-earning couples like teachers and nurses. Details are due at next week's Budget.
items.title: Government raises earnings cap for first-time buyer loan scheme

items.summary: State Bank of India is notifying customers individually after a suspected cyber incident flagged 3,897 records containing personal data. The bank, which received alerts on October 16, assures that funds remain safe and has appointed an independent agency to investigate. While the exposure is confirmed, the bank states the incident has not impacted core operations or financial performance.
items.title: SBI notifies customers after cyber incident flags 3,897 records

items.summary: Storm Austen, named by UK forecasters, is sweeping across northwestern France, bringing violent gusts and severe disruption. Approximately 161,000 households in the north-west, including Brittany and Normandy, lost electricity. The storm has triggered orange alerts in 23 departments and caused transport issues due to fallen trees and strong winds reaching 161 km/h.
items.title: Storm Austen Causes Widespread Power Outages and Disruption in France

items.summary: The State Bank of India stated on Friday that it notified customers via email or WhatsApp following a cyberattack that leaked approximately 3.75 lakh records, including 3,897 containing personally identifiable information. The bank confirmed account balances remain safe and advised vigilance against suspicious communications. This disclosure followed criticism from the Internet Freedom Foundation regarding the bank's initial failure to notify affected individuals.
items.title: State Bank of India Informs Customers After Cyberattack Data Leak

items.summary: Retail sales in Great Britain fell 0.4% month on month in September, steeper than the expected 0.1% drop. The Office for National Statistics reported the decline was driven by poor online clothing sales due to warm weather. Stripping out fuel, sales fell 0.7%. Consumer confidence has fallen at the fastest rate since the pandemic.
items.title: Retail sales in Great Britain fell more steeply than expected last month

items.summary: Fast-fashion retailer Shein agreed to pay US$100 million to settle a US Federal Trade Commission investigation into delivery delays and customer complaints, according to a source with direct knowledge. The settlement represents 44% of the company's second-quarter profit. Shein stated it reached a constructive outcome with the FTC, while the commission declined to comment. The payment follows regulatory scrutiny in Europe and the US, alongside a separate €150 million fine from France's data authority in 2025.
items.title: Shein Agrees to Pay $100m to Settle US FTC Probe

items.summary: The article argues that modern data and AI demands have outgrown traditional Oracle warehouse architectures, which suffer from proprietary formats and high complexity. Databricks promotes its open, unified lakehouse platform as a solution that consolidates analytics, engineering, and AI on a single governed foundation. While acknowledging Oracle's strengths in high-concurrency transactional systems, the text highlights Databricks' cost efficiency and AI capabilities. It cites AXA Japan, which reported a 60% reduction in warehouse costs and 70% lower ETL costs after migrating. Databricks also offers an AI-powered migration agent to automate the transition from Oracle to its platform.
items.title: Databricks Positions Its Lakehouse Architecture as a Modern Alternative to Oracle Data Warehouses

items.summary: A new Space tool allows users to verify if specific Transformers models run unmodified on AWS Trainium. It provides scripts, core counts, and memory usage for selected models. The dataset currently covers text-generation and image-text-to-text models, limited to those fitting on four Trainium2 devices. Users can query the public dataset directly to check results for various compiler and library versions.
items.title: Space Tool Checks Model Compatibility with AWS Trainium

items.summary: RBI data released on Friday indicates that outward remittances by Indians under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme reached $2738.58 million in August 2026. Outflows for overseas equity and debt more than doubled, rising 111 per cent year on year to $321.53 million, accounting for about 11.7 per cent of total LRS outflows. This marks a significant shift in investment patterns compared to the previous year.
items.title: RBI Data Shows Surge in Indian Outward Investment Remittances

items.summary: Microsoft reported that its AI system, MAI-DxO, achieved 83% diagnostic accuracy on complex medical cases, surpassing physicians at 36% with reference materials and 22% without. The results, published in Science, stem from simulated tests rather than real-world practice. Microsoft plans further clinical evaluation with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston.
items.title: Microsoft AI Outperforms Doctors in Simulated Diagnosis Tests

items.summary: Tesla has officially cancelled its plans to build the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand, voiding reservations and promising refunds within 30 days. The decision follows seven years of waiting since customers began paying deposits in 2019. Tesla stated that production plans have been discontinued, citing the high cost of re-engineering the left-hand-drive vehicle for right-hand-drive markets. As a consolation, the automaker is offering a free one-year FSD subscription to those who switch to a Model 3 or Model Y. The move reflects the vehicle's limited global demand and production constraints.
items.title: Tesla Cancels Cybertruck Plans for Australia and New Zealand

items.summary: Tesla India launched a limited-time 'Switch and Save Carnival' offering a Model Y with an effective monthly cost of ₹19,990. This figure requires a ₹6 lakh down payment and subtracts estimated fuel and maintenance savings from the actual EMI of ₹39,990.
items.title: Tesla offers Model Y with low effective monthly cost during limited-time carnival

items.summary: Fort Bend County commissioners approved four agreements offering Tesla up to 35 years of local tax breaks for its proposed $10 billion 'Project Crystal Sun' solar factory. The deals include property tax abatements and incentives contingent on Tesla meeting construction and employment targets. However, Tesla has not yet committed to building the plant in Texas. The agreements cover equipment and inventory, with specific timelines for production and investment. Critics note the thin protections and potential for Tesla to use the offer as leverage in site selection negotiations.
items.title: Tesla's Proposed Texas Solar Factory Faces Uncertain Future Amid Tax Break Offers

items.summary: Tata Motors Ltd returned to profit in the July-September quarter with a net profit of ₹1,254 crore, compared to a loss of ₹867 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 36% to ₹25,338 crore, while sales increased 42% to 135,100 units. The company's EBITDA margin declined to 10.9% due to higher commodity costs. Management expects to integrate Iveco Group into operations by the January-March quarter, pending completion of the tender offer. The company anticipates double-digit industry growth for the full year despite potential moderation from a higher base.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Profit Return and Iveco Integration Plans

items.summary: Anthropic published a report claiming AI adoption has shifted work dynamics, reducing entry-level hiring and increasing reliance on AI agents. CEO Dario Amodei previously predicted AI would eliminate half of entry-level jobs and write 90% of code, but neither occurred. Critics, including researchers Morgan Frank and Julián Posada, question the report's motives, suggesting it aims to boost valuation ahead of an IPO. They note job market declines predated major AI releases and that the report lacks independent auditing. Analysts also point to Anthropic's significant losses and a downgraded credit rating, casting doubt on the company's optimistic claims about productivity and future stability.
items.title: Experts Skeptical of Anthropic's AI Work Report Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Infosys reduced its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1-2% in constant currency terms, down from 1.5-3%, citing weak demand and soft volumes. While AI revenue grew 29% quarter-on-quarter, it accounted for only 10.5% of total revenue. CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka attributed the revision to lower discretionary spending in sectors like software and retail, alongside pricing pressure and higher compensation costs.
items.title: Infosys Cuts FY27 Growth Guidance Amid Weak Demand

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India stated that the Indian economy remains resilient despite global uncertainty, citing strong macroeconomic fundamentals and policy interventions. The IMF subsequently raised India's 2026-27 growth forecast to 7.0%, attributing the increase to robust domestic demand and services activity. The RBI noted that external headwinds are being managed through regulatory measures to curb speculative activity in the foreign exchange market.
items.title: RBI Cites Resilient Indian Economy; IMF Raises Growth Forecast

items.summary: A Reserve Bank of India study introduces a quarterly framework using night-time light satellite data and Google Trends to track economic activity in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Karnataka. This approach aims to provide more timely estimates than the annual Gross State Value Added figures, which typically lag by 12-18 months. The researchers found a strong correlation between night-time light growth and overall economic growth, noting the model complements rather than replaces official statistics.
items.title: RBI Study Proposes Night-Time Light Framework for State Economic Tracking

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's new Greenfield Data Centre in Jatni, Odisha, on October 25. The facility, estimated at Rs 170 crore, aims to boost financial data security and digital infrastructure. Odisha BJP vice-president Jatin Mohanty stated the centre will serve as a backup to the RBI's primary facility in Navi Mumbai and strengthen security for critical financial information.
items.title: PM Modi to Inaugure RBI Data Centre in Odisha

items.summary: The European Central Bank is expected to hold interest rates next week as France's bond sell-off tightens borrowing conditions across the eurozone. ECB President Christine Lagarde stated that solutions to French debt problems must come from Paris, not Frankfurt. France's 10-year government bond yield traded above 5%, widening the gap with German bonds. Moody's is expected to downgrade France's rating, and civil unrest continues. Analysts suggest the bond market has taken over the ECB's job, with yields rising notably and slowing growth. The ECB has played down intervention possibilities but has not ruled them out entirely.
items.title: ECB Faces Pressure as France's Bond Crisis Deepens Ahead of Rate Decision

items.summary: Change.org is rebuilding its platform to shift focus from national viral campaigns to local political action, aiming to solve the feeling that constituents are unheard. New president Steve Dziedzic notes that local petitions are more likely to succeed. The company is investing around $100 million to add AI tools that help draft petitions from social media rants and verify constituent addresses to signal local officials.
items.title: Change.org Rebuilds Platform to Connect Local Petitions with Decision-Makers

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre in Jatni, Odisha, on October 25. Officials stated the visit involves a helicopter transfer and a road trip to the facility. The event marks the PM's ninth visit to the state since the BJP formed the government in 2024. The centre aims to strengthen data management and cybersecurity for core banking functions.
items.title: PM Modi to Inaugure RBI Data Centre in Odisha

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has issued final leverage ratio rules effective April 1, 2027. The central bank proposed a 3.5% ratio for global systemically important banks and other commercial banks, rejecting a request to align with the Basel minimum of 3%. Modifications were incorporated after stakeholder feedback was examined.
items.title: RBI Finalizes Leverage Ratio Rules for Banks Starting 2027

items.summary: OpenAI dismissed three safety researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, on October 1 following an investigation into suspected leaks of sensitive model designs to outside expert Ryan Greenblatt via Signal. The company cites a breach of trust, while the researchers deny wrongdoing, claiming they sought to encourage open collaboration. This incident follows a prior termination of researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner in April 2024 over similar allegations.
items.title: OpenAI Terminates Three Researchers Over Suspected Signal Leaks

items.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg stated that the company's AI agent, Muse, has achieved strong adoption with over 10 million users in the US and Canada. He indicated the tool is central to Meta's monetization strategy, predicting it will generate higher revenue per user than Facebook and Instagram. Zuckerberg noted shopping is the primary use case, with users spending an average of $200 per purchase.
items.title: Meta CEO Zuckerberg Says Muse AI Agent Adoption Is Strong

items.summary: Infosys lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1%-2% from 1.5%-3%, citing deepening weakness in its North American market. The company reported a 1.5% drop in North American revenue, which accounts for over half of its sales, while overall revenue rose 10.7%. CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka attributed the revision to pricing pressure and clients scaling back projects as spending shifts toward AI.
items.title: Infosys Cuts Revenue Forecast Amid North American AI Slowdown

items.summary: NVIDIA outlines a workflow using AI agents to teach the Microduck robot to navigate obstacle courses in simulation. The process involves AI agents like Hermes and Astra creating assets and plans, while NVIDIA Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim handle reinforcement learning and evaluation. The system trains a locomotion policy on ramps and uneven surfaces using parallel simulations on an RTX PRO 6000 GPU. After validation in simulation, the policy is intended for physical deployment, though hardware details remain outside the scope. The workflow connects local planning, cloud-scale learning, and local validation to bridge the gap between simulated and real-world robot behavior.
items.title: NVIDIA Demonstrates AI Workflow for Robot Training in Simulation

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate to 5.50% while injecting ₹2.5 lakh crore into the banking system. SBI Research, in an October 23 report, questioned this dual action, noting three liquidity-injection repo operations from October 19 onwards. The research suggests these moves may send mixed signals regarding the central bank's priority between inflation control and liquidity support, creating market uncertainty.
items.title: RBI Rate Hike and Liquidity Injection Spark Policy Confusion

items.summary: Zoë Baird argues that a Congressional Commission on AI Risk is overdue, noting that major AI developers are warning of potential catastrophic risks and calling for government regulation. While leaders in the industry sound alarms, Congress and the President lack consensus on the government's role. Baird suggests establishing a bipartisan public-private AI Commission to define solutions, citing precedents like the post-Cold War and post-9/11 eras where commissions helped reorient government responses to new threats. She recommends the Commission include congressional leaders, former officials, and independent experts, with a mandate to produce an initial report within six months.
items.title: Zoë Baird Urges Congress to Create AI Risk Commission

items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described a severe crisis involving newly uncovered PHP vulnerabilities that triggered millions of automated exploitation attempts within hours. The flaws, detected using artificial intelligence, prompted emergency patches from the core development team on October 21. Cloudflare data showed attack volumes surged from thousands to millions in just two hours, forcing major corporations and government agencies to shut down services globally to prevent data compromises.
items.title: Microsoft CEO Reacts to Massive PHP Vulnerability Patch Rush

items.summary: American Express plans to cut 5% of its global headcount, affecting approximately 3,500 jobs, as CEO Steve Squeri aims to reduce expenses and improve efficiency. The move follows strong third-quarter earnings but comes amid industry-wide job reductions. Amex also faces a $350 million fine for anti-money-laundering violations, which it says will not impact its 2026 guidance.
items.title: Amex Cuts 5% of Workforce to Cut Costs Amid Rising Expenses

items.summary: The Delhi High Court rejected a plea by AISA president Neha Bora challenging a police notice requiring her to sign a peace bond. Bora argued the notice was vague and lacked factual basis, alleging it was an attempt to suppress dissent. The court proceedings addressed allegations regarding her flag hoisting and participation in protests at Connaught Place and Mandi House.
items.title: Delhi HC Rejects AISA Chief's Plea Against Peace Bond Notice

items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs blamed Beijing for failing to establish peace between India and China, stating that border areas are periodically disturbed when PLA forces deviate from established patrolling patterns. Meanwhile, ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor noted that the force's newly raised Shaurya commando unit demonstrated its capabilities during ongoing face-offs with China's People's Liberation Army in Arunachal Pradesh.
items.title: MEA Blames China for Border Disturbances Amid ITBP Commando Success

items.summary: The Finnish government has granted Posiva an operating licence for the Onkalo final disposal facility and used fuel encapsulation plant. The licence, valid from March 2024 to 2070, allows the disposal of up to 6,500 tonnes of used nuclear fuel from the Olkiluoto and Loviisa power plants. The decision follows a positive safety assessment by the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority (STUK). While the licence is granted, Posiva cannot begin operations until STUK conducts a final inspection. The facility is expected to operate until the 2120s, after which responsibility transfers to the State.
items.title: Finnish Government Grants Operating Licence to Posiva for Nuclear Waste Repository

items.summary: The White House stated that Melania Trump brokered a ceasefire for the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, effective October 29. While the White House claims the truce was secured through direct engagement with Russian and Ukrainian leadership, neither side has officially commented. The city, described as being on the brink of disaster, faces severe humanitarian crises including food shortages and military attacks. Ukraine estimates 6,000 people remain in the area, down from 24,000 before the invasion.
